title: Runbook: Publish Signed Runtime Guarantees with Cost Anchors
creator: Aisha Nandi
description: Establish an operational playbook and automation for publishing Redwood-signed performance claims (latency p50/p95, throughput, normalized unit cost) combined with a cryptographically signed cost anchor and expiry metadata. This ticket captures the product contract, staged validation checks, signer service requirements, ledgering semantics, and rollback triggers that let downstream systems (Console, API, Dedicated routing) depend on a stable, time-bound performance claim. The approach differs from previous 'profile publish' work by introducing: (1) a canonical cost-anchor value (cost per 1k tokens normalized by hw class and sequence mix), (2) an explicit signature/TTL rotation policy, and (3) a lightweight regional variance matrix so clients can pick per-region pins with automated fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Define a signed performance claim schema that includes: profile_id, model_version, hw_class, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, max_throughput_rps, cost_anchor_usd_per_1k, issued_at, expires_at, signer_id, signature
Implement a signer service prototype that can issue signatures for staging profiles and write records to the performance-ledger (append-only) with an audit id
Publish a playbook describing gating thresholds for publish: p95 regression <= 5% vs anchor, throughput >= declared/minimum, unit cost within expected variance
Automate a signed-staging step that mirrors sampled production shadow traffic for 24h and emits a canary report (telemetry links embedded), with a pass/fail decision exported to the Console
Expose the signed claim via the performance catalog API and surface signature metadata in the Console profile UI (issuer, issued_at, expires_at, fingerprint)
Define rollback and isolation procedures: immediate pin to previous signed claim if p95 latency or error rate exceeds rollforward thresholds within first 72h of publish
Document operator runbooks for manual key rotation and emergency unpublish in case of signature key compromise

operational_notes: Signature format example: profile_id:rn:perf:20250301|sha256:9f2e...|issued_by:perf-signer-v2|expires:2025-06-01T00:00:00Z. Cost anchor calculation: compute 1k-token cost using sampled seq distribution, normalize to hw_class baseline (A100-80GB equivalence), and store both raw and normalized values.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signature key compromise could allow forged performance claims. Mitigation: HSM-backed keys, automated rotation, emergency unpublish API, audit trail retention.
Risk: Regional performance variance causing downstream regressions. Mitigation: Publish regional variance matrix and require clients to opt into regional pins or fallback rules.
Risk: Digest mismatch between runtime-observed and published anchors. Mitigation: Shadow validation for 24h and automated sampling-driven re-run before finalize.
Risk: Operational complexity for customers managing many pins. Mitigation: Console 'recommend' layer that suggests best-pin per workload and automated pin-reconciliation job.
